[Fix] openai: Track usage for streaming Harmony Responses

## Motivation

Streaming gpt-oss `/v1/responses` requests report zero terminal usage despite generated content. Populate the streaming context counters used by the final response so clients receive prompt, cache, completion, and total usage.

Related: #41989 covers the non-streaming prompt-token guard; this PR covers the streaming context.

Fixes #45186

## Modifications

- Read the latest available prompt and cached token counts from streaming engine metadata.
- Count completion metadata as a running total within each generation, preserving earlier generations across builtin-tool results.
- Restart the token cursor after a builtin-tool result so the next generation keeps its first tokens in both cumulative and incremental streaming modes.

Production changes are confined to `StreamingHarmonyContext`; buffered Harmony handling and Responses usage assembly remain unchanged. Prompt and cached counts retain the latest-generation convention; the reasoning-token breakdown remains zero.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU validation with Python 3.12.15 and openai-harmony 0.0.4:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python ~/venvs/sg/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_harmony_context.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py -q
```

Our outside-sandbox runs on Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS at `a66e5daa`, against base `ed0b8f43`, passed all 9 original Harmony tests (6 subtests) and all 70 Responses consumer tests (4 subtests). After removing the unused missing-completion fallback and the absent-package import scaffolding, a separate CPU run of the simplified files passed 78 tests and 10 subtests (8 Harmony tests plus the same 70 consumer tests). Direct execution of the simplified Harmony file with `-f`, as CI runs it, passed all 8 tests.

The retained tests cover cumulative/incremental usage, metadata-only terminal chunks, builtin-tool continuation usage, the cumulative token-cursor reset, aborted/incomplete streams, and buffered/non-Harmony controls. Against `ed0b8f43`, the six retained regression methods fail: the usage assertions see zero prompt counts, and the cursor assertion loses the first token after a tool continuation. Both compatibility controls and the zero-token abort/length subcases pass on base.

These tests use prepared engine chunks through the actual context and Responses stream/final-response methods, with the external Harmony parser and encoding mocked. They check delivery of token IDs to the parser, not Harmony parsing itself or a live builtin-tool round trip. No model inference, live server, or dependency-version matrix was run for this fix. The earlier live evidence is from SGLang 0.5.22.

The outside-sandbox OpenAI unit-directory run has pre-existing transcription failures on both base and head. A separate run of `test_serving_transcription.py` reproduced the same five failures and 17 passes on each revision; a direct audio-splitting probe fails because `torchaudio` is missing. This does not involve Harmony. The full directory rerun was not completed in the sandbox.

Repository pre-commit hooks passed outside the sandbox on the changed files at `a66e5daa`. After simplification, the two changed files also passed the repository-pinned Ruff 0.15.1 lint/format checks and isort 7.0.0. No repository-wide `pre-commit run --all-files` result is claimed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This change updates serving-layer usage bookkeeping and resets the parser cursor between builtin-tool generations; it does not change model forward computation.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Changed-file validation is listed above.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable; no configuration or API shape changes.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). CPU regression results are above; model benchmarks were not run.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""Harmony usage bookkeeping with prepared engine chunks and parser/encoding mocks."""
+
+import asyncio
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+
+from utils import (
+    StreamFixture,
+    collect_stream_events,
+    engine_chunk,
+    event_payloads,
+    make_serving,
+)
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import (
+    RequestResponseMetadata,
+    ResponsesRequest,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import reset_context
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class HarmonyStreamUsageTestCase(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        reset_context()
+        self.addCleanup(reset_context)
+        self.processed_tokens = []
+        parser = SimpleNamespace(
+            messages=[], current_content="", process=self.processed_tokens.append
+        )
+        for target, value in (
+            ("get_streamable_parser_for_assistant", parser),
+            ("get_encoding", SimpleNamespace(render=lambda msg: [90, 91])),
+        ):
+            patcher = patch(
+                f"sglang.srt.entrypoints.context.{target}", return_value=value
+            )
+            patcher.start()
+            self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def _context(self):
+        from sglang.srt.entrypoints.context import StreamingHarmonyContext
+
+        return StreamingHarmonyContext(messages=[], tool_sessions={})
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _chunk(ids, completion_tokens, *, prompt=5, cached=1, finish=None):
+        return {
+            "output_ids": ids,
+            "meta_info": {
+                "prompt_tokens": prompt,
+                "cached_tokens": cached,
+                "completion_tokens": completion_tokens,
+                "finish_reason": finish,
+            },
+        }
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _tool_output():
+        from openai_harmony import Message, Role
+
+        return [Message.from_role_and_content(Role.TOOL, "tool result")]
+
+    def _run_stream(self, context, chunks):
+        serving = make_serving()
+        serving.use_harmony = True
+        serving.enable_prompt_tokens_details = True
+        request = ResponsesRequest(model="x", input="hi", stream=True, store=False)
+        metadata = RequestResponseMetadata(request_id=request.request_id)
+
+        async def generate():
+            for chunk in chunks:
+                context.append_output(chunk)
+                yield context
+
+        events = asyncio.run(
+            collect_stream_events(
+                serving.responses_stream_generator(
+                    request,
+                    {},
+                    generate(),
+                    context,
+                    "x",
+                    Mock(),
+                    metadata,
+                    require_reasoning=False,
+                )
+            )
+        )
+        response = event_payloads(events)[-1]["response"]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            response["usage"]["output_tokens"],
+            metadata.final_usage_info.completion_tokens,
+        )
+        return response
+
+    def _assert_usage(self, response, prompt, cached, completion):
+        usage = response["usage"]
+        self.assertEqual(usage["input_tokens"], prompt)
+        self.assertEqual(usage["output_tokens"], completion)
+        self.assertEqual(usage["total_tokens"], prompt + completion)
+        self.assertEqual(usage["input_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"], cached)
+
+    def test_cumulative_usage(self):
+        """Running-total snapshots must not be summed or re-parsed."""
+        context = self._context()
+        response = self._run_stream(
+            context,
+            [
+                self._chunk([11], 1),
+                self._chunk([11, 12, 13], 3),
+                self._chunk(
+                    [11, 12, 13], 3, prompt=8, cached=2, finish={"type": "stop"}
+                ),
+            ],
+        )
+        self._assert_usage(response, 8, 2, 3)
+        self.assertEqual(self.processed_tokens, [11, 12, 13])
+
+    def test_incremental_usage(self):
+        """Delta IDs still carry cumulative completion metadata."""
+        response = self._run_stream(
+            self._context(),
+            [
+                self._chunk([11, 12], 2),
+                self._chunk([13], 3, prompt=8, cached=2, finish={"type": "stop"}),
+            ],
+        )
+        self._assert_usage(response, 8, 2, 3)
+        self.assertEqual(self.processed_tokens, [11, 12, 13])
+
+    def test_metadata_only_terminal_usage(self):
+        """Empty terminal IDs must still update usage, including zero cache."""
+        response = self._run_stream(
+            self._context(),
+            [
+                self._chunk([11, 12], 2),
+                self._chunk([], 3, prompt=8, cached=0, finish={"type": "stop"}),
+            ],
+        )
+        self._assert_usage(response, 8, 0, 3)
+        self.assertEqual(self.processed_tokens, [11, 12])
+
+    def test_tool_continuation_usage(self):
+        """Restarted running totals add to prior generations, excluding tool IDs."""
+        for incremental in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(incremental=incremental):
+                response = self._run_stream(
+                    self._context(),
+                    [
+                        self._chunk([11, 12, 13], 3, finish={"type": "stop"}),
+                        self._tool_output(),
+                        self._chunk([21], 1, prompt=10, cached=2),
+                        self._chunk(
+                            [22] if incremental else [21, 22],
+                            2,
+                            prompt=12,
+                            cached=4,
+                            finish={"type": "stop"},
+                        ),
+                    ],
+                )
+                self._assert_usage(response, 12, 4, 5)
+
+    def test_tool_continuation_resets_cursor(self):
+        """A shorter second cumulative generation must not lose its first IDs."""
+        context = self._context()
+        context.append_output(self._chunk([11, 12, 13], 3))
+        context.append_output(self._tool_output())
+        context.append_output(self._chunk([21], 1))
+        context.append_output(self._chunk([21, 22], 2))
+        self.assertEqual(self.processed_tokens, [11, 12, 13, 90, 91, 21, 22])
+
+    def test_aborted_or_incomplete_usage(self):
+        """Terminal failure/length metadata preserves usage, even before decoding."""
+        for reason, status in (("abort", "failed"), ("length", "incomplete")):
+            for generated in (0, 2):
+                with self.subTest(reason=reason, generated=generated):
+                    chunks = [self._chunk([11, 12], 2)] if generated else []
+                    chunks.append(
+                        {
+                            "output_ids": [],
+                            "meta_info": {
+                                "completion_tokens": generated,
+                                "finish_reason": {"type": reason},
+                            },
+                        }
+                    )
+                    response = self._run_stream(self._context(), chunks)
+                    self.assertEqual(response["status"], status)
+                    self._assert_usage(
+                        response,
+                        5 if generated else 0,
+                        1 if generated else 0,
+                        generated,
+                    )
+
+    def test_buffered_completion_usage_unchanged(self):
+        """Buffered generations accumulate completions independently of streaming."""
+        from sglang.srt.entrypoints.context import HarmonyContext
+
+        context = HarmonyContext(messages=[], tool_sessions={})
+        context.append_output(self._chunk([11, 12, 13], 3))
+        context.append_output(self._tool_output())
+        context.append_output(self._chunk([21, 22], 2))
+        self.assertEqual(context.num_output_tokens, 5)
+        self.assertEqual(context.num_cached_tokens, 1)
+
+    def test_simple_context_usage_unchanged(self):
+        """Non-Harmony streams retain the last engine chunk's usage."""
+        from sglang.srt.entrypoints.context import SimpleContext
+
+        context = SimpleContext()
+        serving = make_serving()
+        serving.enable_prompt_tokens_details = True
+        request = ResponsesRequest(model="x", input="hi", stream=True, store=False)
+        chunks = [
+            engine_chunk("a", 1),
+            engine_chunk("answer", 3, finish=True),
+        ]
+        chunks[-1]["meta_info"].update(prompt_tokens=8, cached_tokens=2)
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            context.append_output(chunk)
+        response = event_payloads(StreamFixture(serving, request).run(chunks))[-1][
+            "response"
+        ]
+        self._assert_usage(response, 8, 2, 3)
+        self.assertIs(context.last_output, chunks[-1])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
